about: The stack split sites (M1.3): every former raylib-equality site and its bucket. compiled: the rule applies to every compiled stack (isCompiledStack); raylib-specific: stays raylib's, Rust gets its own path in the owner package; needs-rust-content: the site needs Rust words or facts, filled by M3.4. Sites are named by file and function, not line.

sites.note: Switched to isCompiledStack: a compiled game without Browser has no Live page.
Switched: a compiled game's web build goes through x.gameBuilds (#servedCompiled); lane-missing notes the console and serves nothing.
Switched to isCompiledStack: Live Reload ends any compiled game's Play window and embedded runs.
Switched to isCompiledStack: a compiled snapshot plays its lane's web build (#playCompiledSnapshot).
Switched: a compiled game's browser export builds through x.gameBuilds (#exportCompiledWeb); lane-missing is build-failed.
Switched: a compiled game is never exported as its raw folder; always through exportPublicCopy.
Switched: no compiled game receives the JavaScript contract; Rust answers its own reason (rustContractKept).
Switched: native.build accepts any compiled game and builds through x.gameBuilds; lane-missing is stack-gated. admissionOf below stays raylib's (Mac bundle, ANGLE) until M3.5.
kind raylib-cpp maps to the raylib template; kind rust-wgpu is a separate branch behind the development gate (core/stack-gate.ts), stack-gated in release builds.
The untargeted-lease backstop stays raylib's; Rust has its own rule: a lease must declare rust-wgpu in preview.acquire {stacks}.

A Rust game's Mac embedded and headless runs go through the wgpu admission and a run directory without ANGLE (playsInOwnWindow/liveEmbedsStack); its window run and Windows/Linux runs stay lane-missing. The Live sender is productized by M3.1.
Gate stays raylib (the app is assembled from a raylib bundle, ANGLE and raylib licences); the build goes through x.gameBuilds. Rust Mac export arrives with the export dispatch table.
Gate stays raylib (zig cross builds, ANGLE, raylib licences); the build goes through x.gameBuilds. Rust Windows/Linux archives arrive with the export dispatch table.
CppSession is raylib's; M3.13 generalizes it into a per-stack compiled session with rustToolchainEnv.
